The paper was published as a NASA Technical Memorandum in 2007.
The research was conducted at the NASA Glenn Research Center.
The paper was presented at the Turbo Expo 2006 conference organized by the American Society of Mechanical Engineers.
The experimental data used in the study was provided by Dr. Tony Arts and Dr. Karen Thole.
Thermal barrier coatings are protective layers applied to turbine blades to insulate them from high temperatures.
The use of thermal barrier coatings can significantly alter the optimal approaches to turbine blade cooling.
The paper discusses various turbine blade cooling approaches, including internal cooling channels, film cooling, and impingement cooling.
Thermal barrier coatings can reduce the heat transfer to the turbine blades, potentially allowing for the use of less aggressive cooling approaches.
The paper suggests that the use of thermal barrier coatings can introduce new challenges, such as the need to manage thermal gradients across the coatings.
The design and implementation of turbine blade cooling systems must be adjusted to account for the presence of thermal barrier coatings.
Factors such as the thermal properties of the coatings and the optimization of cooling approaches must be considered when designing turbine blade cooling systems with thermal barrier coatings.
The potential benefits of using thermal barrier coatings in turbine blade cooling systems include improved efficiency and performance of the turbine system.
